Regression risk on 6 existing approve/deny specs: an unqualified 'collect missing values with ask_user' lets the model raise a form for OPTIONAL fields, blocking the turn so the approval card never appears. FIXED: scoped to REQUIRED, non-inferable values + 'don't ask about optional fields'.

compact_form's hard-cap accounting is an estimate that ignores key/comma overhead; once the size-descending loop reaches entries smaller than a placeholder it GROWS the document while believing it shrinks, and never breaks. FIXED: re-measure the real document each round + stop when elision cannot help.

A ref-free schema over max_bytes fell through to compact_form and was reported schema_form:'defs' with no $defs — contradicting the module's own documented pass-through contract. FIXED: gate the fallback on expansions>0.
Sibling keys beside a $ref were merged UNWALKED, so a subschema-bearing sibling smuggles a #/components/ pointer through, breaking INV-1. FIXED: siblings go through walk_keyword.

The digest is unbounded while the schema beside it is budgeted: no line cap, and follow_defs re-expands a $defs entry at every level. FIXED: DIGEST_MAX_FIELDS + DIGEST_MAX_TEXT_BYTES + an explicit omission marker.

describe emits the schema twice (pretty in text + verbatim in structuredContent) with neither subject to MAX_RESULT_BYTES; the budget measures COMPACT bytes while the text is pretty-printed (~2x). FIXED by the text cap above.

MAX_EXPANSIONS counts refs, not bytes, and the size check runs only after materialisation, so a fan-out DAG is unbounded in peak memory until after the fact. ACCEPTED as a robustness bound, not a security boundary: the input is the app's own in-process OpenAPI document, never attacker-supplied. Recorded, not fixed.

Reach asymmetry: the new walker traverses ~20 keywords to depth 12 while the secret gate schema_has_secret_field_rec stops at depth 6 over 5 keywords, so a secret field reachable only via the wider set would be spelled out to the model without policy denial. 0 live instances verified on the shipped spec. Recorded as a latent posture item; NOT fixed this round (widening the probe is a separate, security-reviewed change).

handlers.rs grew to ~1,940 lines against CODING_GUIDELINES §9's 800-line limit; the digest renderer is generic JSON-Schema-to-prose with no handler dependency. NOT fixed this round — recorded as a follow-up extraction (moving it now would churn the whole diff the audits just reviewed).

The 'single app-side ref resolver' claim holds only under 'app-side': a byte-identical private copy remains in the SDK catalog. NOT fixed — unifying it means exporting from the SDK and re-pointing the secret probe, which belongs with the reach-symmetry work above.

schema_inline is exactly the DB-free class of code chunk C1 moved to the SDK, so placing it app-side splits schema handling across two crates. Recorded; the placement decision (DEC-8) was deliberate for diff-visibility and stands for this round.

walk_keyword is a closed match whose catch-all clones unknown keywords verbatim, so forgetting a subschema-bearing keyword silently leaks a component pointer. Missing today: draft-07 `dependencies`, `contentSchema`, discriminator.mapping (plain strings, not $ref). 0 live instances. PARTIALLY fixed: siblings now walked; the keyword-agnostic post-walk guard is recorded as a follow-up.

The inlined schema is recomputed and re-serialized on every describe call although the catalog is immutable for process lifetime; memoization is trivial. NOT fixed — recorded as a follow-up (real cost is ~10 KB max, and TEST-21's 250 sequential calls complete in seconds).
